questions.q: What makes "I'm not a developer, but I've built FBDI loads and written reconciliation SQL" a strong answer to "how technical are you?"
options: It avoids the question entirely
It claims full software development expertise
It is only acceptable if the interviewer is also a developer
It is precise and specific rather than either inflating or underselling actual technical comfort
questions.explain: The strongest answer is honest and specific - naming real experience (FBDI, SQL, OTBI, BI Publisher) without overclaiming developer-level skill.

questions.q: What is the practical difference between FBDI and a REST API integration?
options: FBDI is batch, loading a prepared file all at once through interface tables; a REST API call is typically real-time, integrating with another live system
They are identical tools with different names
REST APIs can only be used for Payables, never Receivables
FBDI requires no file preparation at all
questions.explain: FBDI suits bulk, periodic batch loads. A REST API call is typically real-time and transactional, suited to live system-to-system integration.

questions.q: In the example reconciliation query in this lesson, what do the returned rows represent?
options: Every account and period in the company, regardless of balance
Only the account/period combinations where the GL balance and the AP subledger total do not match
A list of all approved users in the system
Rows where the GL balance is exactly zero
questions.explain: The WHERE clause filters to rows where the variance (GL balance minus subledger total) is not zero - exactly the accounts and periods that don't reconcile.

questions.q: Which kind of data question should a functional consultant typically own rather than escalate?
options: Performance-tuning a query at enterprise scale
Why a particular transaction should or shouldn't appear in a given account, functionally
Writing new custom integration code
Redesigning the underlying database table structure
questions.explain: Functional meaning - why a transaction belongs where it does, what a status represents - is squarely a functional consultant's territory, unlike development-level technical work.

questions.q: Why does this lesson include a SQL example the reader is only asked to read and explain, not write from scratch?
options: Because functional consultants are never shown SQL in interviews
Because SQL has no relevance to Oracle Financials consulting
Because being able to read and explain someone else's reconciliation query is a realistic, common interview ask for a functional role, distinct from being asked to write it cold
Because writing SQL is strictly a Receivables-only skill
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes being comfortable reading and explaining a query (a realistic functional-consultant expectation) from being asked to author complex SQL unaided, which is a developer-level skill.
